root_cause: The only failing job in this run is a single TensorFlow layer test for Keras LSTM (test_keras_lstm_flags_float32) on CPU, out of 2113 passed tests in the same suite. The triggering commit (#38877) only touches NPU plugin code (WeightlessGraph::create_pipeline, a Coverity NULL_FIELD fix) and has no relation to TensorFlow/Keras LSTM layer emulation on CPU, so the failure is not caused by the commit content. The numeric mismatch (max diff 0.0738) exceeds the FP32 comparison epsilon (1e-4) but is still small relative to the LSTM's recurrent/relu+tanh activation computation, consistent with floating-point accumulation order differences between OpenVINO's LSTM Sequence CPU kernel and TensorFlow/Keras's LSTM cell implementation (e.g., differing gate computation order or fused-op numerics) rather than a logic bug. No other LSTM/Keras-related pattern exists in the knowledge base yet, so this is recorded as a new, likely flaky/low-severity numeric-precision pattern pending repeat occurrences.
reproduction_steps: Build OpenVINO and run the single test locally: `python -m pytest install/tests/layer_tests/tensorflow2_keras_tests/test_tf2_keras_lstm.py::TestKerasLSTM::test_keras_lstm_flags_float32 -k 'flags_float32' -v` after setting up the TF layer tests environment per docs/dev/test_coverage.md. Re-run several times to check for non-determinism; compare OpenVINO CPU LSTMSequence output against the TensorFlow reference with the custom_eps used in layer_test_class.py.
recommended_actions: Re-run the TensorFlow Layer Tests job (or just this test) to confirm whether it is flaky/non-deterministic or a consistent regression.
If it reproduces consistently, bisect recent CPU plugin LSTM/RNN kernel changes (not NPU-related) to find a precision regression.
If it is confirmed non-deterministic/borderline precision, consider widening the FP32 tolerance for this specific LSTM parametrization or marking it as a known-flaky test with a tracking ticket.
Monitor the new pattern (signature_hash da5b0923c1cd0777) for recurrence across future post-commit runs before escalating.
prevention_strategies: For numerically sensitive ops like LSTM/RNN cells, prefer tolerance margins that account for legitimate floating-point summation-order differences between frameworks, and track recurring near-threshold failures as a pattern before treating them as isolated flakiness. Avoid conflating unrelated commits (e.g., NPU-only changes) with CPU TensorFlow layer test failures when triaging.
